main_body: brick forge hearth (rows 14-31) with upper metal chimney hood and shaft (rows 0-13)
top_band: none (the main brick hearth body at rows 14-31 starts directly with vertical brick courses and vertical mortar joints right up to row 14 with no top surface on the hearth shoulders or lintel; the hood cap at rows 1-4 is a flat front plate with corner rivets and a 1px rim at row 5)
evidence: Reading down column x=16 and across the main body: the hood (rows 0-6) is a flat rectangular band with corner rivets at row 3 and a 1px light strip at row 5 (matching the 'column: flat band cap' fail guide), the chimney shaft (rows 7-13) is flat horizontal stripes, and the main brick hearth volume (rows 14-31) is a pure front elevation brick wall where even the exposed left/right shoulders (x=0..5 and x=26..31) show vertical brick courses and mortar joints starting at row 14 instead of a horizontal top surface. The hearth ledge at row 25 is only a 1px line.

style.evidence: Compared to the organic, individually shaded stone masonry on the Beodeul reference (house-h112_0-stone), the forge uses an identical repeating grid of flat 2-tone rectangular bricks, flat horizontal bars across the chimney shaft and hood (rows 1-13), a flat black firebox interior, and a uniform near-black outer outline.
